role: Targeted primary terminology clarification for new definition card, not legal compliance review

sources.title: OECD Test Guideline301 Ready Biodegradability, AnnexI Definitions
sources.locator: AnnexI, physicalPDF56 of62; Primary Biodegradation definition; methods sections distinguish parent-compound analysis from abiotic control
sources.paraphrase: Primary biodegradation requires a chemical structural alteration caused biologically and loss of a specific property. Mineralisation and parent disappearance are distinct endpoints. No current regulatory or pass-threshold claim is made.

sources.title: European Commission CSTEE scientific opinion,25November1999, Definitions
sources.locator: Definitions, Primary Biodegradation; preceding paragraph discusses absence of surface-active properties
sources.paraphrase: The same biological-cause and property-loss boundary is stated in a surfactant scientific context. This corroborates the narrow terminology issue; no legal normativity is derived.
